symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot ping PC2 in VLAN 20 across S1 and S2
topology_note: S1 Fa0/24 trunks to S2 Fa0/24
show_command_output: S1# show interfaces trunk; Fa0/24 trunking native vlan 1; Vlans allowed on trunk 1 10; S2# show vlan brief; 20 Engineering active
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is not allowed on the S1 trunk

symptom: Hosts on VLAN 30 lose connectivity after a new switch is connected
topology_note: S1 Gi0/1 connects to S2 Gi0/1
show_command_output: %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on Gi0/1 (1) with S2 Gi0/1 (99); S1# show interfaces trunk; Gi0/1 native vlan 1
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch between trunk endpoints

symptom: PC3 cannot reach its default gateway from an access port
topology_note: S1 Fa0/8 should be an access port for VLAN 40
show_command_output: S1# show interfaces Fa0/8 switchport; Administrative Mode: static access; Access Mode VLAN: 1 (default); S1# show vlan brief; 40 Finance active
expected_fault: Fa0/8 is assigned to VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 40

symptom: Voice phones register but attached PCs in data VLAN 50 have no access
topology_note: S1 Fa0/12 connects to an IP phone and PC
show_command_output: S1# show running-config interface Fa0/12; switchport mode access; switchport voice vlan 150; S1# show vlan brief; 50 Users active
expected_fault: Data access VLAN 50 is missing from the phone access port

symptom: PC1 can reach peers in 192.168.10.0/24 but cannot reach other networks
topology_note: PC1 is in VLAN 10 with SVI Vlan10 at 192.168.10.1
show_command_output: PC1> ipconfig; IP Address 192.168.10.25; Default Gateway 192.168.1.1; S1# show ip interface brief; Vlan10 192.168.10.1 up up
expected_fault: PC1 has an incorrect default gateway

symptom: All VLAN 20 hosts fail to reach the router despite valid IP addresses
topology_note: S1 provides the VLAN 20 gateway SVI
show_command_output: S1# show ip interface brief; Vlan20 unassigned administratively down down; S1# show vlan brief; 20 Sales active
expected_fault: VLAN 20 gateway SVI is shut down and has no gateway address

symptom: PC2 cannot leave its subnet after a DHCP lease renewal
topology_note: R1 is DHCP server for 10.20.30.0/24
show_command_output: R1# show ip dhcp pool; Pool BRANCH; default-router 10.20.3.1; network 10.20.30.0 255.255.255.0; R1# show ip interface brief; Gi0/0 10.20.30.1 up up
expected_fault: DHCP default-router option does not match the subnet gateway

symptom: New clients receive APIPA addresses on VLAN 10
topology_note: R1 serves DHCP for VLAN 10
show_command_output: R1# show ip dhcp pool; Pool LAN_POOL; Utilization mark is 100%; Leased addresses 50; Free addresses 0
expected_fault: DHCP address pool is exhausted

symptom: Clients on VLAN 30 cannot obtain leases from a server on VLAN 100
topology_note: S1 routes VLAN 30 and DHCP server is 10.100.0.10
show_command_output: S1# show running-config interface Vlan30; interface Vlan30; ip address 10.30.0.1 255.255.255.0; S1# show ip interface Vlan30
expected_fault: DHCP relay helper-address is missing on Vlan30

symptom: Clients receive addresses but cannot communicate with the local network
show_command_output: R1# show ip dhcp pool; Pool USERS; network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.0; default-router 192.168.4.1; R1# show ip interface brief; Gi0/1 192.168.40.1 up up
expected_fault: DHCP pool advertises the wrong default gateway

symptom: A laptop is repeatedly offered an address already used by a printer
topology_note: R1 is the DHCP server for the office LAN
show_command_output: R1# show ip dhcp binding; 192.168.60.20 Automatic; R1# show running-config | include excluded-address; ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.60.1 192.168.60.10
expected_fault: A statically assigned printer address is not excluded from DHCP

symptom: Users can ping 10.10.10.10 but cannot resolve intranet.local
topology_note: DHCP clients use the DNS server at 10.10.10.10
show_command_output: PC1> nslookup intranet.local; DNS request timed out; R1# show ip dhcp pool; dns-server 10.10.10.254
expected_fault: DHCP advertises an incorrect DNS server address

symptom: Clients cannot resolve names after the DNS server was moved
topology_note: R1 provides DHCP on 172.16.5.0/24
show_command_output: R1# show running-config | section dhcp; ip dhcp pool STAFF; dns-server 172.16.5.5; PC1> ping 172.16.5.5; .....
expected_fault: DHCP points clients to an unreachable DNS server

symptom: The web server opens by IP but not by hostname
topology_note: DNS server hosts zone cisco.local at 192.168.70.53
show_command_output: Server# show running-config | include ip dns; ip dns server; ip host portal.cisco.local 192.168.70.70; PC1> nslookup portal.cisco.local 192.168.70.53; ** server can't find portal.cisco.local
expected_fault: DNS zone or host record is missing from the active DNS service

symptom: R1 and R2 do not form an OSPF neighbor relationship
topology_note: R1 and R2 connect on Gi0/0 in area 0
show_command_output: R1# show ip ospf interface Gi0/0; Hello 10 Dead 40; R2# show ip ospf interface Gi0/0; Hello 10 Dead 30
expected_fault: OSPF dead timer mismatch prevents adjacency

symptom: Remote LAN routes are absent from R1 routing table
topology_note: R1 and R2 should exchange OSPF routes on 10.1.12.0/30
show_command_output: R1# show ip ospf neighbor; Neighbor ID 2.2.2.2 FULL; R1# show ip route ospf; Gateway of last resort is not set; R2# show running-config | include network; network 10.2.0.0 0.0.255.255 area 1
expected_fault: Remote LAN is advertised in the wrong OSPF area

symptom: Two routers remain in OSPF EXSTART state
topology_note: R1 and R2 share an Ethernet segment
show_command_output: R1# show ip ospf neighbor; 2.2.2.2 EXSTART/DROTHER; R1# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 | include MTU; MTU 1500; R2# show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 | include MTU; MTU 1400
expected_fault: OSPF interface MTU mismatch prevents database exchange

symptom: Branch users cannot reach headquarters after a static route change
topology_note: R1 reaches HQ through next hop 172.16.12.2
show_command_output: R1# show ip route 10.50.0.0; S 10.50.0.0/16 [1/0] via 172.16.21.2; R1# show ip interface brief; Gi0/1 172.16.12.1 up up
expected_fault: Static route uses an unreachable next-hop address

symptom: R3 has duplicate routes and intermittent OSPF reachability
topology_note: R1 and R3 are in area 0 with loopbacks
show_command_output: R1# show ip ospf neighbor; 3.3.3.3 FULL; R3# show ip ospf | include Router ID; Routing Process "ospf 1" with ID 1.1.1.1; R1# show ip ospf | include Router ID; Routing Process "ospf 1" with ID 1.1.1.1
expected_fault: Duplicate OSPF router IDs cause unstable routing behavior

symptom: Management PC cannot SSH to R1 but can ping it
topology_note: R1 VTY access should permit 192.168.10.0/24
show_command_output: R1# show access-lists; Standard IP access list 10; 10 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255; R1# show run | section line vty; access-class 10 in
expected_fault: VTY ACL excludes the management subnet

symptom: Web users cannot reach an internal HTTP server
topology_note: ACL 101 is applied inbound on R1 Gi0/0
show_command_output: R1# show access-lists 101; 10 deny tcp 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.10 eq 80; 20 permit ip any any; R1# show ip interface Gi0/0 | include access
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies HTTP traffic to the server

symptom: DHCP relay packets are dropped between VLANs
topology_note: R1 filters traffic inbound from the client VLAN
show_command_output: R1# show access-lists 110; 10 deny udp any any eq 67; 20 permit ip any any; R1# show run interface Gi0/1; ip access-group 110 in
expected_fault: ACL blocks DHCP server UDP port 67

symptom: Users can browse HTTPS but DNS lookups fail
topology_note: R1 applies ACL 120 toward the DNS server
show_command_output: R1# show access-lists 120; 10 deny udp 192.168.80.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.90.53 eq 53; 20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL blocks DNS UDP port 53

symptom: Internal hosts can ping the ISP gateway but cannot browse the internet
topology_note: R1 connects LAN Gi0/1 to ISP Gi0/0
show_command_output: R1# show ip nat statistics; Total active translations: 0; Inside interfaces: Gi0/1; Outside interfaces: Gi0/0; R1# show run | include ip nat inside source
expected_fault: Dynamic PAT overload rule is missing

symptom: Internet-bound traffic leaves the LAN untranslated
topology_note: R1 is the enterprise edge router
show_command_output: R1# show run interface Gi0/0; ip nat inside; R1# show run interface Gi0/1; ip nat outside; R1# show ip nat statistics; Total active translations: 0
expected_fault: NAT inside and outside interface roles are reversed

symptom: Only 192.168.100.0/24 users cannot access the internet
topology_note: R1 should translate the 192.168.100.0/24 LAN
show_command_output: R1# show access-lists 1; Standard IP access list 1; 10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255; R1# show run | include ip nat inside source; ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/0 overload
expected_fault: NAT source ACL does not include the affected LAN

symptom: Laptop sees Cisco-Corp SSID but WPA2 authentication fails
topology_note: WLC WLAN 1 serves corporate clients
show_command_output: WLC# show wlan summary; 1 Cisco-Corp UP WPA2 PSK Key Cisco123!; Laptop log: Connecting with PSK cisco123!; Auth failed
expected_fault: Wireless client PSK does not match the WLAN PSK

symptom: Wireless clients authenticate but never receive an IP address
topology_note: WLC maps WLAN 5 to VLAN 200
show_command_output: WLC# show wlan summary; 5 Guest UP VLAN 200; S1# show interfaces trunk; Gi0/2 trunking; Vlans allowed on trunk 1 10 20
expected_fault: Wireless VLAN 200 is not permitted on the WLC switch trunk

symptom: Clients cannot discover the branch SSID after an AP change
topology_note: WLC manages AP-BRANCH
show_command_output: WLC# show ap summary; AP-BRANCH Registered; WLC# show wlan summary; 10 Branch-WiFi DISABLED WPA2; Client scan: no Branch-WiFi found
expected_fault: The Branch-WiFi WLAN is disabled on the controller

symptom: Connected wireless users cannot reach internal servers
topology_note: WLC guest WLAN should use VLAN 210 and gateway 10.210.0.1
show_command_output: WLC# show wlan summary; 12 Corp-WLAN UP VLAN 210; S1# show ip interface brief; Vlan210 10.21.0.1 up up; Client> ipconfig; Default Gateway 10.210.0.1
expected_fault: Wireless VLAN gateway SVI is addressed for the wrong subnet
